researchReflections.2026-03-27: My research right now focuses on emotions, specifically how emotions are constructed in the brain. Going against the classic model of emotions where they are things that occur to us, constructionism posits that our brains are actually constructing emotions based on context, past events, and physiological signals. For instance you might have the same exact feeling in your stomach and body before you get on a rollercoaster as you have before you step up for a huge presentation. One of these experiences gets constructed as excitement and the other as anxiety.

cnNotes.title: ePAT - Interoception State vs Trait Writeup Guide
cnNotes.body:
## Section 1, the theoretical question, ~250 words. 
Open with the contested question: is interoceptive accuracy a stable individual-difference trait or a state that varies within-person with momentary context? Cite Murphy and Bird (2024) for the trait position — their "auditing measures" paper explicitly argues for classification stability across situations as the meaningful construct. 
Cite Barrett's constructionist work and Lindquist's papers on emotion construction for the state position — interoceptive perception as constructed in the moment from bodily signals plus conceptual scaffolding plus context. Frame the disagreement as theoretically substantive (not just methodological), with each position making specific predictions about what within-person variability across ecological contexts should look like. 
End the section with the meta-claim: this disagreement has been unresolvable empirically because no measurement tool has existed that combines PAT-family validity with within-person ecological repeatability.

## Section 2, predictions under each account, ~250 words. 
Under the trait account: within-person variance should be near measurement-noise floor, between-person variance should dominate, EMA state variables should be uncorrelated with classification. Under the state/constructionist account: within-person variance should be substantial, EMA state variables should systematically predict classification, specific predictions like arousal decreases accuracy (sensory flooding), focus increases it, comfort is orthogonal, social context matters via attentional competition.
 Be specific. Vague predictions are unfalsifiable, and unfalsifiable predictions are how state-account papers get correctly criticized for unfalsifiable theorizing. The more specific you can be, the more your eventual finding means something.

## Section 3, why ePAT uniquely enables this test, ~250 words. 
Prior interoception work in EMA used HCT (invalid). PAT 2.0 exists but requires native app installation, validates only at rest, and is not designed for repeated within-person assessment. ePAT inherits PAT 2.0's task validity (you implement the same paradigm with the same dual-method scoring) while adding browser-based zero-install deployment, URL-personalized session links, and a session structure designed for repeated ecological administration. 
The methodological contribution is justified by the theoretical contribution — ePAT exists because the theoretical question requires it, not as an end in itself.

cnNotes.title: Shoebox Post
cnNotes.body:
I built a thing and I don't really know what to call it. It's not quite a journal; a journal is where you go to think, and this is where you go to save things you've already noticed. Closest I can get is 'a commonplace book for small moments,' but that's a mouthful. Let me just describe what it does!
For some context, I am a longtime lurker, first real post. I want to share something I made for myself and just put on the App Store today. It's free, there's no account, no server, no subscription. I'll explain what it does and why, and you can decide if it's for you.
The problem I was trying to solve: my weeks had lost their texture. If you'd asked me what happened last Tuesday, I could give you "work, gym, dinner" and almost nothing else. Not because nothing happened, but because I wasn't 'encoding' any of it. Days were collapsing into a blur in memory even though they felt fine while I was living them.
I looked at the existing journaling apps and bounced off all of them. Streaks, notifications, AI coaches, mood charts, subscriptions, prompts like "how was your day?" that are so broad they're useless. I wanted something closer to a physical shoebox under the bed, somewhere to drop small things I'd otherwise forget, and nothing else.
So I decided to build shoebox. Here's the actual mechanism it's built around, because I think it matters more than the feature list:
Your brain mostly ignores things it predicts. This is why commutes disappear from memory and why the tenth time you walk past a mural you stop seeing it. Attention follows prediction error, the stuff that surprises you, however slightly. The problem is that in a normal day there's plenty of prediction error happening; you're just not flagging it as worth noticing, so it never makes it into memory.
Shoebox tries to hijack that in the gentlest way possible. Each morning it gives you one very specific prompt. Not "how was your day," but things like:
a five-minute friendship
a sudden change in the lighting or weather
a detail most people probably walked right past
the exact moment your energy shifted today
You don't have to answer it. You're not supposed to sit and think about it. You just read it once in the morning and close the app. That's the whole interaction. What the prompt does is prime your attention. The same way that if I tell you to notice red cars, you'll see red cars all day. Your brain spends the rest of the day quietly scanning for the thing, and in the process it catches a bunch of other small moments it would normally have filtered out. When one lands, you open the app, type a sentence, close it. Ten seconds.
Over weeks, two things happen. The obvious one: you accumulate a feed of small, specific moments from your own life. On a bad day you can scroll it slowly, one card at a time, and it's genuinely grounding and proof that your life isn't actually a blur, you just weren't looking. The less obvious one: the priming effect starts running on its own. After a while your attention defaults to noticing, and you don't really need the prompts anymore. At that point you can keep logging or delete the app. I built it assuming you'd eventually leave.
A few things that matter for this sub specifically:
No server. It syncs through your own iCloud. I cannot read your entries. There is no analytics SDK, no crash reporter phoning home, nothing.
No streaks, no notifications, no gamification. Skip a day, skip a month, use it only on hard days, use it as a gratitude list, use it as a sensory journal. There's no correct way and nothing pesters you if you stop.
No ads, no subscription, no paid tier. It's free. I'm not trying to build a business on this. In fact, only losing money with my dev account!
iOS only, sorry Android users, it's a solo project and SwiftData/iCloud is what let me build it without a backend. Maybe I will consider it with enough support!
Short notes on the design: the feed is built to be scrolled slowly, one memory per screen, like flipping through index cards in a shoebox. That part was deliberate as fast infinite scroll would defeat the whole point. It has a (imo) beautiful and satisfying clicking as you scroll through your memories as well as a shuffle button to randomly be reminded of a past memory.
If any of this resonates, the link is below. I'd genuinely love to hear what prompts work for you and which ones fall flat, since the prompt list is the thing I'll keep tuning. Really, I will take any feedback!

cnNotes.title: EMA-PAT Writeup (old)
cnNotes.speaker: ePAT
cnNotes.body:
# The Idea
Building off the idea of a [[Custom EMA software stored locally]] and Jingyi's suggestion to look into the PAT, I decided to [[Revamp phone HBD app]] and create ePAT

To look into the PAT I made use of two open source applications. The first was the actual phase adjustment task - https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0301051121001642, https://github.com/huma-engineering/Phase-Adjustment-Task
- This task was built using swift architecture to run on iOS devices
  - ## Issues
    - No ability to pair PAT performance with momentary self-report (EMA)
    - App distribution logistics (TestFlight invites, device compatibility) created overhead
    - Couldn't modify or extend without iOS development expertise
    - this method also relied on precompiled libraries with large sizes

To overcome these obstacles I also looked into web based 'ppg' heart rate detectors finding this website 
- https://heartrate.netlify.app/
  - this is a simple netlify app that worked on my device, checked using my AirPods Heartrate detectors for accuracy and found similar results
  - this website also used an open source GitHub repo so others could use the code
    - https://github.com/richrd/heart-rate-monitor

Building off of both of these public repos I decided to tackle the challenge this way -
- rebuild the original PAT using javascript and HTML
  - this way it could be run on the web without participants having to download any additional software or complications with compilation of the app etc
  - it also allows for changes during the study and easily implemented
    - as soon as I press deploy on GitHub, a few seconds later the applet website should update
- Allow for PAT to be tasked within an in-house EMA 'software' (surveys hosted not through EMA apps)
- allow for javascript linking at the end of sent links (?id=1&session=pat) leading to ability for participants to receive a simple text that brings them to the study without having to fiddle with any external software or apps

Once I had combined the two I realized I could not actually deploy the PAT task without their arbitrary library, so I created a simpler version that detects the same thing - heart beat peaks through finger color detection

This all leads to what was actually built - **The ePAT** 

# The ePAT (Ecological Phase Assessment Task)
## Architecture decisions
- Single HTML file — entire application (UI, task logic, beat detection, audio engine, motion detection, data export) in one self-contained document
- Zero dependencies, zero build step, zero backend required for basic operation
- Hosted on any static file server (Firebase Hosting free tier, GitHub Pages, institutional web space)
- Participants access via URL link in Safari — no installation, no app store, no TestFlight
- URL parameter routing (?session=pat vs ?session=ema, ?id=XX) enables dual-task deployment from a single codebase

## PPG beat detection — WABP onset detection
- Replaced proprietary BioBeats library with a custom JavaScript implementation
- **Algorithm**: Port of the WABP algorithm (Zong et al., 2003; PhysioNet) adapted for camera PPG
  - Operates on the half-wave rectified first derivative (positive slopes only) of the bandpass-filtered PPG signal
  - Moving sum over a 130ms slope window produces a "slope energy" signal with bumps at each pulse upstroke
  - Adaptive dual-threshold system (Ta/T1) with 8-second learning period for self-calibration
  - Backward onset search from threshold crossing to find the pulse wave foot (onset), not peak
  - Eye-closing lockout (250ms) prevents within-beat double detections
  - Additional 400ms minimum IBI guard at the BeatDetector layer to reject dicrotic notch reflections (the secondary pressure wave bump that appears 300-400ms after onset, outside WABP's eye-closing window)
  - Threshold decay if no pulse found in 2.5 seconds — prevents the detector from going silent after transient signal loss
- **Why onset, not peak**: Onset detection finds a consistent fiducial point on the upstroke. Peak detection finds local maxima which shift with pulse wave morphology. The PAT 2.0 refinement paper (Palmer, Murphy, Bird et al., 2025 preprint) moved to beat-triggered tones, making consistent onset timing more important than matching the subjective "thump" sensation
- **Why not predictive scheduling**: PAT 1.0 predicted the next beat time from a rolling HR estimate and scheduled tones ahead. PAT 2.0 explicitly abandoned this (listed as refinement #1) because prediction error from sinus arrhythmia compounds with detection latency. Beat-triggered tones have only a constant detection delay, which is estimable and correctable
- Camera → red channel mean extraction → IIR bandpass filter (0.67–3.33 Hz, dynamically tuned to actual framerate) → WABP onset detection with adaptive thresholds
- Finger presence detection via brightness range + red channel dominance ratio with debounce
- Per-beat callbacks with instantaneous and average BPM/period — same contract as the original Swift HREventsDelegate protocol
- Torch activation with multi-camera fallback for cross-device compatibility (skips iOS virtual dual/triple cameras to lock a physical lens)
- Fully inspectable, tunable, and documented — every threshold is a named constant
- All WABP time constants (eye-closing, slope window, learning period, threshold decay) rescale dynamically based on actual camera framerate

## Dynamic framerate and processing loop
- Camera `getUserMedia` requests `frameRate: { ideal: 120, min: 30 }` — gets 60fps on most iPhones, 120fps on some flagships, never worse than 30fps
- Actual framerate read back from `track.getSettings()` after stream acquisition; stored in session data for analysis
- Bandpass filter coefficients (HP_ALPHA, LP_ALPHA) recomputed for the actual framerate — fixed coefficients at wrong sample rate distort the frequency response
- Processing loop uses `requestVideoFrameCallback` when available (Chrome, Safari) — fires once per decoded video frame, so at 120fps video you get 120 processing cycles regardless of display refresh rate. Falls back to `requestAnimationFrame` on Firefox
- Higher framerate directly improves onset timing precision: ±33ms at 30fps → ±17ms at 60fps → ±8ms at 120fps

## Signal quality diagnostics
- Frame timing tracking: every frame logs inter-frame delta, computes effective FPS (median-based, more accurate than `getSettings()`), flags drops where dt > 2× expected interval
- ISP clipping detection: tracks frames where brightness saturates high (>0.95, ISP cranking gain) or low (<0.05 with finger present, ISP underexposing). Clipping crushes the AC pulse component
- Group delay estimation: analytical computation of bandpass filter group delay at 1.2 Hz (typical cardiac fundamental) for the actual framerate and filter coefficients
- All diagnostics logged per-trial and per-baseline as `ppgDiagnostics` object in the JSON output:
  - `negotiatedFPS`, `effectiveFPS`, `totalFrames`, `frameDropCount`, `frameDropRate`
  - `frameDeltaMedianMs`, `frameDeltaIQRMs` (jitter)
  - `clipHighFrames`, `clipLowFrames`, `clipRate`
  - `estimatedGroupDelayMs`
- These enable principled exclusion criteria and covariate analysis in R rather than hoping the data is clean

## Phase adjustment task — faithful port with PAT 2.0 alignment
- Beat-triggered tone scheduling (PAT 2.0 approach, not PAT 1.0 predictive scheduling)
- Knob-to-delay mapping preserved: delay = (averagePeriod / 2) × knobValue
- Trial structure: 2 practice + 20 real trials
- Confidence rating (0–9 scale) after each trial
- Body map localization every 4th trial
- Data output arrays (instantPeriods, averagePeriods, knobScales, currentDelays, instantErrs) match original structure for R pipeline compatibility
- Detection algorithm tagged in session data (`detectionAlgorithm: 'wabp_onset'`)

## Additions beyond the original
- EMA integration: Daily check-in surveys (body connection, stress, physical sensation free-text) accessible via URL parameter, enabling within-person interoceptive self-report alongside objective PAT measurement
- AudioContext precision scheduling: Tones scheduled via Web Audio API clock (sub-millisecond precision) instead of setTimeout (1–16ms jitter) — critical because the dependent variable IS temporal offset
- Tone timing ground truth: Each beat logs beatDetectedAt, beatTime, intendedDelay, and scheduledAt — enables post-hoc jitter quantification and methods-section reporting
- Finger loss event logging: Timestamped {lostAt, restoredAt} pairs per trial for principled exclusion criteria
- Baseline validation: Minimum beat count threshold (80 beats in 120s) with automatic restart — prevents garbage baselines from propagating into task
- Initial knob position logging: Random start position recorded per trial for anchoring effect analysis
- Motion detection: Accelerometer-based movement warnings during trials
- Wake lock: Prevents screen dimming during extended recording
- PPG diagnostics: Per-trial frame timing, clipping, and group delay data for signal quality QC

## Known platform limitations vs. native app
- **No ISP control**: Cannot disable auto-exposure, auto-white-balance, or auto-focus in JavaScript. The native Huma app locks these for the finger-on-lens scenario. Mitigated by diagnostics (clipping detection, frame drop tracking) enabling post-hoc QC
- **Audio latency**: Web Audio API has 5-20ms non-deterministic latency through the browser audio graph vs. CoreAudio/AAudio in native apps. Constant per-session, so doesn't affect consistency scores, but limits absolute delay comparisons across platforms
- **Variable framerate**: Mobile ISPs can drop frames or reduce framerate when the lens is occluded. Mitigated by frame timing diagnostics but not preventable from JavaScript. The native app can lock the camera pipeline
- **No cheat-avoidance mechanism (yet)**: PAT 2.0 uses a lock-drag-confirm interaction + 1000ms idle abort to prevent pulse-checking. Not yet implemented. Less critical for supervised lab sessions (our protocol) than unsupervised remote administration

## PAT 2.0 alignment status
| Feature | PAT 2.0 | ePAT | Status |
|---------|---------|------|--------|
| Beat-triggered tones | ✅ | ✅ | Done |
| Onset detection (not peak) | ✅ | ✅ (WABP) | Done |
| Multi-camera handling | ✅ | ✅ | Done |
| Cheat-avoidance (lock-drag-confirm) | ✅ | ❌ | Planned for post-pilot |
| Screener task (two-tone matching) | ✅ | ❌ | Planned for post-pilot |
| Trial replacement (invalid → new trial) | ✅ | ❌ | Planned for post-pilot |
| Delay-based consistency scoring | ✅ | ❌ (R pipeline needed) | Next priority |
| Individualised classification thresholds | ✅ | ❌ (R pipeline needed) | Next priority |
| Classification-only (not continuous scores) | ✅ | ❌ (R pipeline needed) | Next priority |
| Confidence ratings per-trial | ✅ | ✅ | Done |
| Body map every 4 trials | ✅ | ✅ | Done |

# Next Steps

## Immediate — reach out to Ren Palmer
- Co-author on PAT 2.0 preprint, met at SAS
- Ask about: edge cases they encountered, whether OSF analysis code (osf.io/fp5sq) is final version, practical advice on browser-based deployment
- Mention: building browser-based PAT for longitudinal EMA, cite their work, interested in her input before piloting
- Sets up collaborative relationship; browser-based deployment may be interesting to their group

## This week — internal testing
- Run self + 2-3 lab members through full flow (onboarding → baseline → 20 trials → JSON download)
- Don't look at BPM display during trials (simulate naive participant)
- Check JSON output: IBIs in 600-1100ms range, no suspiciously short intervals, ppgDiagnostics.frameDropRate acceptable
- Test on at least one iPhone AND one Android device

## Next — R scoring pipeline (PAT 2.0 analysis)
- Build before piloting so you can evaluate data quality
- Implement both scoring methods:
  - **Phase-based consistency**: delay as proportion of IBI, consistency across trials (PAT 1.0 method)
  - **Delay-based consistency**: raw delay in ms, consistency across trials (PAT 2.0 primary method)
- Implement individualised classification thresholds: simulate 100 random responders with same IBI distribution per participant, take 95th percentile as cutoff
- Classification output (interoceptive / non-interoceptive), NOT continuous scores — PAT 2.0 recommendation
- IBI variability QC: flag participants with IBI SD > 0.36s across trials
- Use OSF example code from Palmer et al. as reference

## CNAP validation
- Run self through full PAT while connected to CNAP
- Visual comparison: do IBI streams track the same signal?
- Assess whether detection latency is fixed offset vs. variable jitter
- The tone-before-pulse perception during validation testing is EXPECTED and CORRECT — WABP fires at pulse wave onset (~100-200ms before the peak pressure you consciously feel at the wrist)
- If erratic: tune detection thresholds before proceeding
- If consistent: plan formal validation with 5-10 lab members

## Formal validation protocol
- N = 4-5 lab members, full PAT while CNAP-connected
- Sync method: physical tap creating simultaneous arterial response (CNAP) and accelerometer event (phone)
- Compute: IBI correlation, beat-by-beat concordance, detection latency distribution (mean, SD, skew)
- Report detection jitter and frame timing diagnostics
- Determine if fixed-offset correction is needed

## Pre-pilot technical fixes (informed by internal testing)
- Add baseline restart counter with progressive guidance after repeated failures ("Try pressing more firmly")
- Consider adding signal quality indicator during trials (not just baseline)

## Post-pilot — PAT 2.0 task design features
- Cheat-avoidance mechanism (lock-drag-confirm + 1000ms idle abort)
- Screener task (separate HTML file, two audio tones, no camera needed)
- Trial replacement logic (invalid trials → restart with new random phase, continue until 20 valid)
- Only implement after signal processing is validated and pilot data confirms the foundation is solid — don't layer task-design changes on top of unvalidated signal processing

## Current Setup
- https://ema.keeganwhitacre.com - normal study, end of URL will determine if EMA or ePAT test
- https://ema.keeganwhitacre.com/validation.html - validation tool to test reliability of data
- https://ema.keeganwhitacre.com/onboarding.html - onboarding with preferences setting, consent, instructions, testing calibrations, etc

# Summary
- What I started with: 
  - A lab-locked iOS app dependent on a proprietary beat detection library, requiring in-person sessions and iOS development expertise to maintain.
- What I built: 
  - A zero-infrastructure, browser-based tool that runs the same psychophysical task with WABP onset detection, precision audio scheduling, dynamic framerate adaptation, signal quality diagnostics, and integrated EMA capability — deployable to any participant with a phone and a link.
- What makes it different from a straight port:
  - It's not the Huma app in a browser. It's a browser-native implementation that uses a published, referenced beat detection algorithm (WABP; Zong et al., 2003), is embedded in a longitudinal EMA design for ecological interoception research, and is fully open source with inspectable signal processing. The PAT was published so other researchers could use it — this is that.
- What it opens up: 
  - Ecological interoception research, within-person variability analysis, and the ability to test constructionist predictions about body awareness that weren't feasible with single-session lab measurements.
- What's needed next: 
  - Reach out to Ren Palmer (PAT 2.0 co-author, met at SAS). Build R scoring pipeline with PAT 2.0 delay-based consistency and classification. CNAP validation of beat detection. Pilot with 10-15 participants. IRB approval for cloud-based data collection.

## Ideas
- Some sort of feedback, either fun fact about constructionism or "you have contributed *N* beats to the study!" altruism
- Consider pre-seeding the R scoring pipeline with the PAT 2.0 OSF analysis code before collecting any data — you need it to evaluate whether the signal processing is working

cnNotes.speaker: Wormwood et al.
cnNotes.body:
**One-line summary:**
- Emotion fluency was not associated with emotion granularity, but was associated with greater negative affective intensity and variety.
 
**What I'd challenge:**
- The validity of the emotion fluency task, with an only 0.52 test-retest reliability
 
**What I'd steal for my own work:**
- Participants choose which 5 days they would like to receive the survey, with the caveat of one day having to be weekend.
 
# Journal Club Notes
- Verbal fluency correlations with SES, income, etc
- Not just people's knowledge of words driving their granularity
- Emotion Fluency task - what words come first vs later in the task?
- Verbal Fluency Task - get to category they are very familiar with and then get really into that category, animal breeds vs emotion task (happy and then into more details of happy etc)
- Expertise vs having a lot of words
- Katie Hoemann - words (20) of emotions, unlimited time, different breakdowns across cultures - 
 
## Emotion Fluency Task in EMA
- once a day/ or less emotion fluency task
- what moment level things influence what comes to mind
 
### Lisa
- Granularity not associated because the measure is not about context and using the right words
- Language is the way we measure something more complex
- tailoring a category of possible futures to a single instance - metabolic advantages
 
- Granularity is not using million dollar words, but instead analogies for context specific construction of experiences
- use of sad and angry in specific contexts vs lots of words that are more specific but not relevant
- Words are not the main point
- which features of words are important
 
 
- Words are invitations for a conversation, have no meaning on their own
- "periodic table is not real" - simplified construct, can't use it on its own
- dictionary definitions are abstractions of the meaning
